sections.title: Setting up Levix
sections.text:
Levix is a WhatsApp bot you run yourself. It links to your own WhatsApp account
by scanning a QR code, exactly like WhatsApp Web, and everything after that is
configured from a control panel in your browser.

There is no configuration file to edit. There are no keys to generate. If a
guide anywhere tells you to create a `.env` file, it is out of date.

---

sections.title: What you need
sections.text:
- A computer or a small server that stays on. A Raspberry Pi is enough.
- **Node.js 24** — nodejs.org, pick the Node 24 LTS
  build. A newer Node also starts, with a warning that only Node 24 is
  supported. (Or skip Node entirely and use Docker, below.)
- A phone with WhatsApp, to scan the QR once.

Levix stores everything in one file using SQLite, which Node 24 includes.
Nothing is compiled, nothing else is installed, no database server is needed.

---

sections.title: The quickest way
sections.text:
```bash
npm install -g levix-bot
levix
```

`levix-bot` is the npm package name. The command you run after installing it is
still just `levix`.

The terminal prints something like:

```
  Levix is running

  Panel: http://localhost:3001/setup
  Data:  ~/.levix

  First run — that link asks you to pick a password.
  Opening it from another machine also needs this code:

  [Setup] Setup code: 43CB5162

  Opening Levix in your browser...

  Not linked to WhatsApp yet? Open the panel, go to Connection and
  press Start session.

  Press Ctrl+C to stop.
```

1. On a desktop the browser opens by itself. Otherwise open that address.
2. Choose a password. (Opening the page from a *different* machine also asks
   for the setup code above — that's what stops a stranger from claiming your
   bot before you do.)
3. You land on the control panel. Go to **Connection**, press **Start session**,
   and scan the QR with WhatsApp → Settings → Linked devices → Link a device.
   A brand-new install does not begin pairing until you press Start.
4. Send `!ping` in any chat. The bot answers.

After that first successful pairing, the saved WhatsApp session resumes
automatically after a Levix, Docker or systemd restart. You only need the
Connection screen again if you deliberately stop/unlink the session or WhatsApp
requires a new link.

Levix only opens a browser when there is one to open: over SSH, under systemd,
in Docker or in CI it just prints the address and says why. `--no-open` turns
it off anywhere.

That's the whole setup. Keep the terminal open, or see *Keeping it running*.

If the panel files are missing, the basic English setup and login forms still work.
Run `npm run build:frontend` from a source checkout or reinstall Levix to restore
the full panel and QR screen.

---

sections.title: With Docker instead
sections.text:
No Node install, nothing on your system but the container:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Abdodiab2005/levix
cd levix
docker compose up -d
```

Then open <http://localhost:3001>. The setup code is in the logs:

```bash
docker compose logs levix | grep -F '[Setup] Setup code:' | tail -1
```

Everything the bot owns lives in the `levix-data` volume. Once WhatsApp has
been paired, restarting the container reuses that saved session automatically.

---

sections.title: Running it without the web panel
sections.text:
On a server you may not want a panel at all:

```bash
levix headless
```

That starts the bot and nothing else — no web interface, no port opened. If the
bot has never been paired it prints the QR straight into the terminal:

```
  Levix — headless

  No WhatsApp session found.

  Scan this QR from:
  WhatsApp -> Linked devices -> Link a device

  [ the QR ]

  ✓ WhatsApp connected
  ✓ Levix is ready

  [command count] commands loaded
```

You can switch modes freely: the data directory is the same either way.

---

sections.title: Putting it on a domain
sections.text:
```bash
sudo levix domain bot.example.com
```

Levix looks at what the server already runs and fits in with it:

| What it finds | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| nginx (+ certbot) | adds one nginx site, runs `nginx -t`, reloads, offers HTTPS |
| Caddy | adds one site file to the existing Caddy |
| Apache | prints the reverse-proxy settings; changes nothing |
| a hosting panel (Plesk, cPanel, CloudPanel, …) | prints the settings and where to enter them; changes nothing |
| nothing at all | offers to install Caddy, which handles HTTPS by itself |
| something unrecognised on :80/:443 | stops and tells you what is there |

It never edits another site, never overwrites `nginx.conf`, and never reloads a
configuration that failed validation. Running it twice does not create a second
copy of anything.

The bot itself never needs root — only this command does, and only when it is
actually going to write to `/etc`.

---

sections.title: Turning on the parts that need a key
sections.text:
The bot works out of the box. Two features need a free key, and both are set in
**Settings** in the panel — never in a file:

| Feature | Where to get the key |
| --- | --- |
| AI replies (`!gemini`, `!ai`) | aistudio.google.com/apikey |
| Weather (`!weather`) | openweathermap.org/api |

Paste the key, press Save. It applies to the next message — no restart.

---

sections.title: Keeping it running
sections.text:
Closing the terminal stops the bot. Pick one:

**Docker** — already handled; the container restarts by itself.

**A Linux server** — the installer sets up a service that starts on boot:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://levix.leviro.net/install.sh | bash
```

Opening the panel from your laptop counts as another machine, so it asks for
the setup code. Print it with:

```bash
journalctl -u levix --no-pager | grep -F '[Setup] Setup code:' | tail -1
```

Read the script first if you like — it is short, and it explains each step.

That always installs the newest stable Levix. To stay on this release — the
same script, pinned — use its own URL:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://levix.leviro.net/install/v4.9.0.sh | bash
```

**Behind a proxy** — if this server reaches the internet through a proxy, the
panel has a **WhatsApp proxy** section under Settings: protocol (HTTP, HTTPS or
SOCKS5), host, port, and a username and password if yours needs them. It applies
to the WhatsApp connection only — the panel itself and the AI keep connecting
directly. Saving it never interrupts a working session; the Connection screen
offers **Reconnect to apply** when a change is waiting.

**Your own machine** — `pm2` works well:

```bash
npm install -g pm2
pm2 start levix --name levix
pm2 save && pm2 startup
```

---

sections.title: Where your data is
sections.text:
One directory holds all of it: the database, the WhatsApp session, the bot's
long-term memory, the logs.

```bash
levix where
```

- installed with npm: `~/.levix`
- running from a git clone: `./data` inside the clone
- Docker: the `levix-data` volume

A copy of this directory, taken while Levix is stopped, is a full copy: it holds
the WhatsApp pairing and the encryption key, so keep it private. On another
device WhatsApp may still ask you to pair again. For an encrypted backup without
the pairing, use **Settings → Backup** (below).

sections.title: Back up and restore
sections.text:
Open **Settings → Backup**. Create a backup with a password of at least 12
characters and save the `.levixbak` file. Keep the password safe: Levix cannot
recover it. To restore, upload the file, enter its backup password, review the
preview, then confirm with your panel password.

The preview lists what the restore changes: settings and API keys that are
added, replaced or unchanged, the ones the backup does not hold (they stay as
they are), the AI persona, and the WhatsApp account data. When the restore would
replace or remove something this install already has, tick the confirmation
before **Confirm restore** is enabled. Restore writes only what the backup
holds: a setting, an API key or a persona missing from the backup keeps its
current value. It keeps this install's panel password, recovery email, session
key, device settings and encryption key. WhatsApp pairing is never in the backup;
pair the account again by hand. Conversations, AI memory, stickers, schedules,
roles and group data activate only when the same WhatsApp account connects.
If a different account connects, the Backup screen shows **waiting account
data**. You can later pair the matching account or choose **Discard** to remove
the waiting data.

---

sections.title: When something goes wrong
sections.text:
**"Port 3001 is already taken"** — Levix is already running, or something else
holds that port. Open <http://localhost:3001> and see. To move it: Settings →
Server → Control panel port, then restart.

**Forgot the panel password**

Two ways to get a one-time reset code without touching the terminal:

- **WhatsApp code** — on the login screen, choose **WhatsApp**; the code arrives
  in your own chat with the bot. Needs the WhatsApp session up.
- **Recovery email** — if you added and verified an address under **Settings**,
  the same screen offers **Email**, and the code goes to that address. It is
  delivered by a Levix mail relay, which emails the code and keeps neither the
  address nor the code in readable form. Adding the address in Settings asks
  for the panel password. Ten wrong codes in a day pause reset for a day.
  If email recovery needs verification again, sign in using WhatsApp recovery or
  the CLI alternative below, then verify the address in Settings. Older saved
  addresses also need this one-time verification after upgrading. Verifying an
  address again disables email recovery on other installations using that address.
  Authorization expires after 365 days without an accepted email-reset request;
  network and mail-service outages do not remove your saved recovery settings.

If the session is down and neither can arrive, `levix reset-password` still
works from the terminal:

```bash
levix reset-password
```

Then start it again and pick a new one. The WhatsApp link is untouched.

**The bot stopped answering** — WhatsApp dropped the link, usually because the
phone was offline for a long time. Open the panel; if it asks for a QR, scan it
again.

**"levix-bot needs Node 24"** — your Node is older. Install the Node 24 LTS
build from nodejs.org and try again.

**"Warning: Node 26… is newer than Node 24"** — Levix still runs. Only Node 24
is built and tested, so help with problems on a newer Node is best effort.
Install Node 24 LTS for a supported setup.

**Start over completely** — stop the bot, delete the data directory
(`levix where` prints it), start it again. That wipes everything: settings,
memory, the WhatsApp link.

---

sections.title: Two things worth knowing
sections.text:
**Whoever scans the QR owns the bot.** That account is the owner and can run
every command. You can add more owners and admins from **Roles** in the panel.

**The panel has no HTTPS of its own.** On your own machine that's fine. On a
server reachable from the internet, run `sudo levix domain bot.example.com` —
it puts a reverse proxy with a certificate in front, sets the proxy-hop count
for you, and stops the panel listening publicly on its raw port.

sections.title: Levix for Android
sections.text:
Run **Levix** directly on your Android phone as an autonomous background companion — **no VPS, no Termux at runtime, no cloud server, and no subscription fees**.

Levix for Android packages the complete Levix stack into a standalone Android APK:
- **Node.js 24 LTS** compiled for Android Bionic (ARM64 **and** ARMv7)
- **SQLite** datastore powered by Node's built-in `node:sqlite`
- **Baileys v7** WhatsApp protocol engine with local LID mapping
- **AI Agent** with multi-provider support (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic)
- **All 69 commands** & group moderation tools
- **Embedded FFmpeg** for native WhatsApp voice notes (`!tts`) and video/image preview thumbnails
- **Local Web Control Panel** accessible only inside the app's built-in WebView; a phone browser cannot open it

---

sections.title: Requirements
sections.text:
| Requirement | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Architecture** | **ARM64** (`levix-android-arm64.apk` — almost all phones since 2016) or **ARMv7 32-bit** (`levix-android-armv7.apk` — remaining 32-bit-only devices). |
| **Android Version** | **Android 10** or newer (API level 29+; the app targets API 36). |
| **Free Storage** | ~400 MB (APK ~100–110 MB per ABI + unpacked app bundle + SQLite database). |
| **WhatsApp Account** | An active WhatsApp account to link with via pairing code or QR. |

---

sections.title: Installation
sections.text:
1. Go to the Levix Releases page on GitHub.
2. Download the APK that matches your device:
   - **`levix-android-arm64.apk`** — 64-bit devices (almost all phones since 2016).
   - **`levix-android-armv7.apk`** — 32-bit-only devices.
   - Not sure? Install the AIDA64 app or check your phone's specs; if it says `arm64-v8a` / `aarch64` / "64-bit", use the arm64 build.
3. Open the downloaded APK on your device and tap **Install**.
   - If prompted by Android, enable **"Install unknown apps"** for your browser or file manager.
4. Open the **Levix Host** app from your home screen or app drawer.

---

sections.title: Step 1: Grant Permissions & Start the Host
sections.text:
1. Launch **Levix Host**. The first launch runs a short guided tour over the home screen: it dims the page, highlights one real button at a time and explains it in a card. **Back**, **Next**, **Done** and **Skip** are on the card, so the tour never leaves you stuck. **Show guide again** on the home screen replays it.
2. Tap the big circle (**Start Assistant**).
3. When prompted, grant **Notification** permissions so the host can maintain an ongoing foreground service and keep the bot running while the screen is off.
4. When prompted, tap **Allow** to disable battery optimization for Levix.

The circle becomes a progress state while the engine starts. Once ready, **Connect WhatsApp** opens the secure Connection workflow. Engine readiness and WhatsApp connectivity are shown separately, and the ongoing notification reports the session state.

sections.title: Step 2: Set Admin Password
sections.text:
1. Tap **Connect WhatsApp** in the app to open the panel on Connection. Once fully connected, the home action becomes **Open Control Panel**.
2. The initial setup screen will appear (`/setup`). Choose a secure master password for your web control panel and submit.

sections.title: Step 3: Link WhatsApp via Pairing Code (Recommended)
sections.text:
Because you are running the bot on a phone, scanning a QR code on the same screen is difficult. Levix provides a direct **Pairing Code** option:
1. In the Web Control Panel, navigate to **Connection**.
2. Select **Pairing Code** (selected by default on Android).
3. Enter your WhatsApp phone number with international country code (e.g. `201012345678` — do **not** include `+`, `-`, or leading `0`).
4. Tap **Request Pairing Code**.
5. An 8-character code will be generated (e.g., `ABCD-1234`).
6. On your phone, open **WhatsApp**:
   - Tap **Settings** (or the three dots menu `⋮`).
   - Tap **Linked Devices**.
   - Tap **Link a Device**.
   - Tap **Link with phone number instead** at the bottom of the screen.
   - Enter the 8-character code displayed in your Levix panel.
7. WhatsApp will complete the handshake. Within a few seconds, the connection status will turn green: **Connected**.

sections.title: The home screen
sections.text:
- **Header** — the Levix mark and app name stay on the left; the language and appearance controls stay on the right in both languages. Tap the globe to switch **العربية** / **English**, and the sun/moon to switch Light / Dark.
- **Start Assistant** — the large power circle is the primary action while stopped. Startup shows progress, pairing offers **Connect WhatsApp**, and a connected assistant shows a compact ready card with **Open Control Panel**. **Stop Assistant** is a separate action. Contextual guidance also explains reconnecting, offline pauses, expired sessions, and engine errors.
- **Battery Guard** — appears below activation guidance. Restrictions show a warning and **Enable Battery Guard**; an exemption shows a compact healthy card. Android or device restrictions can still interrupt background operation.
- **WhatsApp & Bot Engine tiles** — tap the WhatsApp tile for the read-only connection sheet: state, since when, error, network and engine.
- **Media Hub** — browses the statuses and WhatsApp media stored on this phone.
- **Show guide again** — replays the guided tour, highlighting each control on the home screen in turn. Controls that are hidden in the current state are skipped.
- **Diagnostics** — tap the card for **Save & open** (writes `Downloads/Levix/levix-host-<timestamp>.log` and opens it in your viewer) or **Share logs** (Android's share sheet). Nothing leaves the phone until you pick one.

---

sections.title: Keeping Levix Running in the Background
sections.text: Android manufacturers apply aggressive battery-saving algorithms that kill background processes. To keep Levix connected 24/7 with the screen locked:

sections.title: Xiaomi / Redmi / POCO (HyperOS / MIUI)
sections.text:
1. Open **Settings** → **Apps** → **Manage apps** → **Levix**.
2. Enable **Autostart** (or **Background autostart**).
3. Tap **Battery saver** → select **No restrictions**.
4. Open the Android **Recents** screen (app switcher), press and hold the **Levix** card, and tap the **Lock icon** to lock it in memory.

sections.title: Samsung Galaxy (One UI)
sections.text:
1. Open **Settings** → **Apps** → **Levix**.
2. Tap **Battery** → select **Unrestricted**.
3. Open **Settings** → **Battery** → **Background usage limits** → **Never sleeping apps** → tap `+` and add **Levix**.

sections.title: OnePlus / OPPO / Realme (OxygenOS / ColorOS)
sections.text:
1. Open **Settings** → **Apps** → **App management** → **Levix**.
2. Tap **Battery usage** → enable:
   - **Allow foreground activity**
   - **Allow background activity**
   - **Allow auto-launch**

sections.title: Google Pixel / Motorola / LineageOS / Stock Android
sections.text:
1. Open **Settings** → **Apps** → **Levix**.
2. Tap **App battery usage** (or **Battery**) → select **Unrestricted**.

---

sections.title: Real-Time Notifications & Offline Handling
sections.text:
Levix includes intelligent network and connection lifecycle handling:

- **Ongoing Foreground Notification**:
  The notification drawer displays the live state of both the host service and WhatsApp:
  - `WhatsApp: Connected`
  - `WhatsApp: ⏳ Reconnecting (code: reason)`
  - `WhatsApp: ⏸️ Paused (No Internet)`
- **Offline Alerts (`levix-alerts`)**:
  If your phone loses Wi-Fi and mobile data or WhatsApp disconnects, Levix posts a high-priority alert. When internet returns, the alert automatically dismisses.
- **Smart Pause & Auto-Reconnect**:
  When you enter airplane mode or lose connectivity, Levix immediately pauses retries instead of burning your 5 retry attempts. As soon as connectivity is restored, Levix resets the retry counter and automatically reconnects within 2 seconds.

---

sections.title: Media Hub
sections.text:
Open **Media Hub** from the native host screen to browse WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business statuses, photos, videos, voice notes, audio, documents, and stickers. Search, filter, favorite, share, and save copies to user-visible Levix folders. Storage Insights shows local totals and large files. Only copies saved by Levix can be deleted in the hub.

The header has compact source, media-type, filter, sort, and Storage Insights icons. Tap a choice icon to see its options. Long-press a card to select it; its border covers the whole preview. The selection bar keeps Save, Share, and Delete as icons, with Select all, Favorite, sticker actions, and Clear selection in the three-dot menu.

The hub asks for media permission when you open it, after an explanation. Android 14's selected-media permission shows only the items you selected; you can select more or allow full access in system settings. Hidden `.Statuses` folders and some documents may not appear in MediaStore. In that case, use **Enable status access** to grant read-only access to the WhatsApp Media folder through Android's folder picker. Levix remembers the grant and asks again only if access is removed. Media Hub never uploads files, names, thumbnails, or folder details.

Levix bundles a native build of **FFmpeg** (`libffmpeg.so` — ARM64 or ARMv7, matching the APK) inside the APK, compiled from source with NDK r29 so it is safe on 16 KB-page devices.
- **Voice Notes (`!tts`)**: The Text-to-Speech command automatically transcodes Google TTS MP3 audio into true WhatsApp PTT voice notes (`audio/ogg; codecs=opus`).
- **Media Previews**: Video and picture thumbnails (`jpegThumbnail`) are generated locally on the phone before sending, ensuring crisp previews in chat bubbles and quotes.
- **Stickers**: The WebP encode, animation and muxing that Sticker Studio needs (see below).
- No external packages or Termux setup are required.

---

sections.title: Sticker Studio
sections.text: Sticker Studio is the panel's sticker screen. It is reached from the native side rather than opened by hand, because the panel runs in a WebView with no file picker of its own and no way to reach a `content://` URI belonging to the Media Hub.

sections.title: The two actions in the Media Hub
sections.text:
Any single item in **Media Hub** can be turned into a sticker, in two places:

- the **viewer**, on the action row under the picture — hidden for items with no sticker form;
- the **selection bar’s three-dot menu**, on **Make sticker** — offered only when exactly one stickerable file is selected, since Sticker Studio takes one file at a time.

The label follows the file:

| Label | When | What the panel does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Make sticker** | an image, GIF or video | opens the converter: trim, frame, and re-encode to WebP |
| **Add to stickers** | a WhatsApp sticker (`.webp`) | keeps the file as it is and only adds it to your library |

Voice notes, audio and documents get no action at all — they have no sticker form, so nothing is shown rather than something that would always refuse.

Tapping either one opens the panel on its Sticker Studio screen. Nothing is read on the phone at that moment: the app records the URI it already has permission to read, and the panel picks it up from there. If the file is over the cap, or Android never reported its size, you get a message instead of a screen.

sections.title: Source and export transfers
sections.text: The Media Hub offers files up to 16 MB, mirroring Sticker Studio's server upload limit (`src/stickers/limits.cjs`, `UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES`). It still rejects items with unknown size before opening the panel. This is an offer rule, not a WebView bridge limit: Android streams the selected `content://` URI to Node over the local unix socket, and Node enforces the upload limit again while reading. The panel receives a short-lived token and a loopback preview URL. A preview GET opens the URI as a stream in `shouldInterceptRequest`; no source file is copied into the bridge.

sections.title: Sticker Studio host methods
sections.text:
| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `takePendingSticker()` | One-shot Media Hub hand-off; returns `intent`, `token`, `url`, `name`, `mime`, and `size`, with no bytes |
| `pickStickerSource(callId)` | Opens Android's image/video picker, then returns source metadata through `window.__levixHostDone` |
| `uploadSource(callId, token, fileName, maxBytes)` | Streams the selected URI to the local Sticker Studio upload route |
| `exportFile(callId, action, path, method, jsonBody, fileName, mime)` | Streams an export from Node to the share cache or Downloads/Levix |
| `cancel(callId)` | Closes an active transfer and returns a cancelled result |
| `pickFile(callId)` | Opens an openable document and returns a source token and metadata |
| `uploadBackup(callId, token, maxBytes)` | Streams the picked document to `POST /dashboard/api/backup/restore/uploads` with exact length |
| `saveBackup(callId, token, fileName)` | Opens Create Document and streams `GET /dashboard/api/backup/exports/<64 lowercase hex>` to it |

The asynchronous methods acknowledge immediately and deliver small JSON through `window.__levixHostDone(callId, result)`. Tokens expire after one hour; the activity keeps at most eight and clears them when it closes. Share files are written to `cache/shared/` and swept after 24 hours. Save writes a pending MediaStore Downloads row and publishes it only after the stream finishes. Both export destinations enforce the Sticker Studio MIME allowlist and sanitize the file name.

Backup bytes never enter JavaScript. Backup upload reports progress through
`window.__levixHostProgress(callId, bytes, total)` and requires a known size up
to 16 GiB. Backup save uses Android's document picker; cancellation or transfer
failure deletes a created partial document where the provider permits it.

The ordinary `request()` bridge still carries other panel POST bodies; the small settings JSON export still uses `saveExportFile()`.
Re-editing a sticker from the library creates its upload on the server, so its preview Blob is never posted through the bridge.

sections.title: The FFmpeg components this needs
sections.text:
`android/scripts/build-ffmpeg-android.sh` builds **libwebp 1.6.0** (with a pinned SHA-256) and adds these components:

| Kind | Components | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| libraries | `libwebp` + `libwebpmux` + `libsharpyuv` | WebP encode/decode, animation, and muxing; libwebp's own sharp/colour-space helpers |
| encoders | `libwebp`, `libwebp_anim`, `rawvideo` | still stickers, animated stickers, and raw frames |
| demuxers | `rawvideo`, `image_gif_pipe` | reading GIF frames to animate them |
| muxers | `webp`, `rawvideo` | writing a `.webp` container |

Static and PIC, `CC`/`AR`/`RANLIB` supplied by the cross toolchain, so the result stays position-independent and safe on 16 KB-page devices. The ARM64 binary grows by roughly 5% against the build without it.

The filters FFmpeg already enables at defaults are what the studio's own pipeline needs — `pad`, `fps`, `scale`, `crop`, `trim`, `transpose`, `split`, `colorkey`, `overlay`, `palettegen`, `paletteuse` — so nothing was added or removed there.

---

sections.title: Data Management & Backups
sections.text:
All state is stored in your device's private app storage:
```text
/data/data/net.leviro.levix/files/data/
├── levix.db           # SQLite database (settings, auth creds, notes, schedules)
├── levix.key          # Key for sealed API keys and WhatsApp session data
├── logs/              # Bot activity logs
└── memory/            # AI long-term memory markdown files
```

sections.title: Backing Up Your Data
sections.text:
- **Settings → Backup (recommended)**: create an encrypted `.levixbak` file with
  a password of at least 12 characters, then save it with Android's save picker
  (Download, Drive or any document provider you choose). It holds bot settings,
  command setup, API keys, the AI persona, conversations, memory, schedules,
  group data, roles and stickers. It never holds the WhatsApp pairing, the panel
  password, the recovery email, `levix.key` or Android preferences. To restore,
  open the file with the Android picker, enter its password, review what the
  restore adds or replaces, confirm, and link the same WhatsApp account by hand.
  Settings, API keys and a persona the backup does not hold keep their values.
  Levix never uploads a backup anywhere. See SETUP.md.
- **Via Root / File Manager** (full copy, including the WhatsApp session):
  Copy the whole `/data/data/net.leviro.levix/files/data/` folder to private storage.
  `levix.db` alone cannot restore API keys or the WhatsApp session: both are
  sealed with `levix.key` in the same folder. Anyone holding both files can
  read those secrets, so keep the copy private.

---

sections.title: Upgrading
sections.text:
To update Levix to a newer version:
1. Download the new APK from Releases — `levix-android-arm64.apk` or `levix-android-armv7.apk`, whichever you installed before.
2. Install it directly over the existing app.
3. Your database, WhatsApp pairing, settings, and passwords will remain completely intact.
4. On first launch after updating, Levix automatically detects the version upgrade and refreshes the application bundle in the background.

---

sections.title: Building the APK from Source
sections.text: If you prefer to compile Levix Host from source:

sections.title: 1. Prerequisites
sections.text:
- **JDK 17** & **Android SDK 36** (`$ANDROID_HOME` configured)
- **Node.js 24** on your development machine (the version in `.node-version`)
- Tools: `zip`, `unzip`, `rsync`, `curl`, `python3`, `make` and `pkg-config` (for building FFmpeg). `dpkg-deb` is needed only for `--build-archive`, not for a default build. `--update-pins` needs `curl` and `python3`.

sections.title: 2. Fetch the Embedded Node.js Runtimes (ARM64 + ARMv7)
sections.text:
Download and unpack the Node.js 24 binaries for Android and build FFmpeg for each ABI (the first run downloads NDK r29 unless `$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/29.0.14206865` exists):
```bash
android/scripts/fetch-node-android.sh                 # both ABIs
android/scripts/fetch-node-android.sh arm64-v8a       # one ABI only
```
The runtime comes from `levix-node-runtime-24.22.1-android.tar.xz`, a release asset pinned by sha256 in `android/scripts/node-runtime.lock`. The script downloads that one file, checks its sha256 and size, then extracts the ABI through `node-runtime-archive.py`, which checks `MANIFEST.json`: schema 1, Node 24, the package rows in `termux-packages.lock` (package, version, sha256, url), every file sha256, and every symlink target. It never contacts Termux and never falls back to another Node.

The script verifies every 64-bit ELF is safe on 16 KB-page devices — 16 KB aligned, RELRO not sharing a page with writable data, built with NDK r28+ — as Google Play requires for apps targeting API 35+, and fails the build otherwise.

Each staged runtime is stamped (`~/.cache/levix-android/node-runtime/<abi>/.levix-stamp`) with the sha256 prefixes of `build-ffmpeg-android.sh`, `fetch-node-android.sh`, `termux-packages.lock`, `node-runtime.lock` and `node-runtime-archive.py`. Gradle recomputes the stamp and refuses to package a runtime staged from older recipes or pins, one whose `libffmpeg.so` lacks the `libwebp`/`libwebp_anim` sticker encoders, or one whose `libnode.so` is not the Node version in the lock, and prints the command that refreshes it (`LEVIX_ANDROID_ABIS=<abi> bash android/scripts/fetch-node-android.sh`). Re-run the script whenever a recipe or a lock changes; Gradle will not run it for you.

sections.title: Rebuilding the runtime archive
sections.text:
Maintainers refresh the deb pins with `bash android/scripts/fetch-node-android.sh --update-pins` while Termux still serves Node 24, then build the archive with `bash android/scripts/fetch-node-android.sh --build-archive`. Publishing the new release asset needs the owner's approval; after it is published, put its file name, sha256, size and URL in `android/scripts/node-runtime.lock`. The archive build is deterministic, so a rebuild from the same pinned debs gives the same sha256 with the same Python and liblzma. Every file is checked against the manifest either way.

A default build uses the cached copy when its sha256 matches `node-runtime.lock`, and otherwise downloads the release asset. If that download fails it prints the URL and stops. It never rebuilds the archive by itself. Maintainers rebuild with `bash android/scripts/fetch-node-android.sh --build-archive`. The recovery order for them is: the release asset; any cached copy with the pinned sha256; that rebuild from the pinned debs; otherwise an owner decision, because Termux may stop shipping Node 24.

sections.title: 3. Build the APKs
sections.text:
Run Gradle to assemble one APK per ABI:
```bash
cd android
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug
```
> The Gradle `stageLevixApp` task automatically runs `npm run build:frontend` to compile the React dashboard into `public/dashboard`, stages the production server bundle into `levix-app.zip`, and embeds it inside the APK assets. Staging fails rather than packaging an APK whose panel would render unstyled: it checks that `public/dashboard/index.html` exists, links a stylesheet, and that every asset it references is present both on disk and inside `levix-app.zip`.

The archive holds production dependencies only. They are installed from `package-lock.json` into a separate directory, checked by `check-stage-deps.mjs`, and written by `zip-tree.mjs` as a byte-reproducible zip. `node scripts/size-report.mjs <apk|aab>` prints the component sizes, and CI adds that table to each run's summary.

> The panel's CSS is built for the system WebView, which on the 32-bit (`armeabi-v7a`) devices the APK supports is far behind current desktop browsers. `frontend/vite.config.ts` flattens Tailwind's `@layer` blocks — a WebView without cascade layers (pre-Chrome 99) drops them wholesale and renders the panel with no styling at all — and downlevels `oklch()` through Lightning CSS.

> It also re-states Tailwind's `translate`/`rotate`/`scale` utilities as `transform` behind `@supports not (translate: 0px)`. Those standalone properties need Chrome 104, and a WebView that drops them leaves the mobile sidebar parked over the page (its `-translate-x-full` never moves it off-screen), the settings toggles stuck showing "off", and the RTL icon flips dead. The build fails rather than emit a transform it cannot downlevel, so a Tailwind upgrade that uses a new shape is caught here instead of on someone's phone.

Outputs land in `android/app/build/outputs/apk/<buildType>/` as `levix-android-arm64.apk` and `levix-android-armv7.apk`.

sections.title: 4. Install onto Device
sections.text:
```bash
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/levix-android-arm64.apk
```

sections.title: 5. Build the Google Play bundle (AAB)
sections.text:
Google Play requires an **AAB**, not an APK:
```bash
cd android
./gradlew :app:stageLevixBundle
# -> app/build/outputs/bundle/release/levix-android.aab
```
The AAB contains both ABIs; Play generates the right per-device APK from it. Sign with your upload keystore via `LEVIX_KEYSTORE_FILE` / `LEVIX_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` / `LEVIX_KEY_ALIAS` / `LEVIX_KEY_PASSWORD` (`stageLevixBundle` refuses to run without them — Play rejects debug-signed bundles; release APKs from `assembleRelease` still fall back to the debug keystore for local testing). Before submitting, fill the Play Console **Data safety** form from `PRIVACY.md` and host that policy at a public URL.

---

sections.title: Sending Feedback & Reaching the Developer
sections.text:
Levix has no support desk, and nothing about your installation is reported
automatically. When something is wrong — or right — the panel is where you say so:

1. Tap **Open Control Panel** in the app.
2. Go to **Settings → Feedback**.
3. Pick what it is about (a bug, an idea, a question, or how it is going), write
   the message, and press **Send**.

The message goes to the developer directly. What travels with it: your text, the
topic, an optional 1–5 rating, an optional way to reach you, one optional file
you attach yourself (a screenshot or a log, up to 20 MB), and the Levix version
and platform so a bug report says which build it came from. Nothing from
WhatsApp is attached — no message, chat, contact, credential or key — and nothing
is sent until you press Send. The same form is on the web at
levix.leviro.net/feedback if the host will
not start at all.

Leave the contact field empty and nothing you send names you; fill it in if you
want an answer. For a bug you would rather see tracked in public with logs
attached, open a GitHub issue
and use **Diagnostics → Share logs** in the app to attach the host log.

---

sections.title: Why did WhatsApp show "Couldn't link device" when using a pairing code?
sections.text: Make sure you enter your phone number with the international country code and without leading zeroes or symbols (e.g. `2010XXXXXXXX` for Egypt, `1XXXXXXXXXX` for USA). Do **not** enter `010...` or `+20...`.

sections.title: Why does the Web Control Panel say "Connection Refused"?
sections.text: Make sure the host service is running. Open the Levix Host app and verify the Bot Engine card shows that the engine is operational. If it is stopped, tap the big circle (**Start Assistant**).

sections.title: Can I access the Web Control Panel from my PC on the same Wi-Fi?
sections.text:
No. The Android panel listens on a private socket file, not a TCP port. By
design, it is reachable only inside the Levix app; other devices and other
apps cannot reach it.

sections.title: Does Levix work on 32-bit (armv7) phones?
sections.text: Yes — install **`levix-android-armv7.apk`**. (Most phones from 2016 onward are 64-bit and should use `levix-android-arm64.apk` instead; the 64-bit build is the one Google Play serves by default.)

sections.title: How do I report a bug or ask for a feature?
sections.text:
**Settings → Feedback** in the control panel — see "Sending Feedback & Reaching
the Developer" above. It reaches the developer directly, and the app version and
platform travel with it so nothing has to be guessed.

sections.title: Will Levix drain my battery?
sections.text: Levix is optimized to idle at negligible CPU usage (~0.1% - 0.5% CPU when no messages are being processed). RAM usage typically hovers around 90–140 MB.

sections.title: Levix Privacy Policy & Google Play Data Safety
sections.text:
> **Effective date:** 2026-11-02
> **Applies to:** the Levix Android app (`net.leviro.levix`) and the Levix
> self-hosted server distributed from this repository.
> **Product:** Levix, built by Abdelrhman Diab, Leviro.

---

sections.title: Plain-language summary
sections.text:
Levix is a **self-hosted** personal WhatsApp bot. The Android app runs the
entire bot **on your device** — there is no Levix cloud, no Levix account, and
no Levix server. The developer does **not** receive any data from your
installation on its own: no analytics, no telemetry, no ads, and no automatic
crash reporting. The only things that ever reach **Leviro Support** (the
developer's support channel) are the ones **you** choose to send: a message in
**Settings → Feedback** (and the optional diagnostics block you can tick on that
form), and a crash report you press Send on in the panel. Nothing is transmitted until you do. A Levix-operated mail
relay delivers a recovery code only when you ask for one. It keeps keyed hashes
for verification, authorization and rate limiting, never the readable address,
code or token, and it does not send the address to the developer.

Data leaves your device while WhatsApp is linked, when a command or AI feature
runs, or when you enable an optional setting or take a panel action. Gemini's
Google Search grounding is enabled by default for Gemini AI requests; Gemini
decides whether to search for each answer.

1. **WhatsApp** — Levix is a WhatsApp client; your messages, pairing data and
   WhatsApp account credentials necessarily travel to WhatsApp (Meta) so the
   product can function.
2. **Your chosen AI provider** — when you use an AI feature, the prompt and
   relevant context are sent to the provider you configured with **your own API
   key** (Google Gemini, any OpenAI-compatible server, or Anthropic). Depending
   on the feature and provider, that context can include your display name,
   WhatsApp user/phone identifiers, group name, message text, quoted or
   mentioned participant identifiers, AI history or long-term memory, and
   media or files you ask the AI to process. Supported images can be sent to
   OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic providers; Gemini can additionally receive
   supported video, audio and documents. Speech-to-text can send audio to
   Gemini or an OpenAI-compatible provider. Natural-language `generate_image`
   requests use the dedicated Gemini image endpoint/key/model, including when
   chat uses OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic. `transcribe_audio` uploads only
   audio attached to or quoted by the invoking message, after checking the
   sender's transcription permission. Its transcript is returned to the chat
   provider to prepare the answer and can be stored in local AI conversation
   history. That chat provider can differ from the transcription provider.
3. **Search and web pages:** Gemini can run Google Search grounding inside
   its request when it decides current information is needed. The AI's
   `web_search` and `search_news` tools send queries to `html.duckduckgo.com`,
   or Google Programmable Search when configured. `search_wikipedia` sends a
   query and matching page titles to `ar.wikipedia.org` or `en.wikipedia.org`.
   `fetch_url` requests the HTTPS page the AI opens from that page's host.
4. **Leviro Support, if you send feedback** — the panel's **Settings → Feedback**
   form sends what you typed (your message, the topic, an optional 1–5 rating,
   an optional contact), one optional file you pick yourself (a screenshot or a
   log, up to 20 MB), plus the Levix version and the platform it runs on. If —
   and only if — you also tick **Attach device & technical diagnostics**, it
   additionally sends the diagnostics listed in section 2a. It travels through
   `levix.leviro.net/api/feedback`. Leviro Support currently receives it through
   Telegram, as a Telegram message, or as a Telegram document when a file is
   attached, so Telegram carries and stores that message. A private Leviro
   Support dashboard is planned to replace the Telegram delivery; this policy
   will change with a new effective date when it does. Nothing
   is attached from WhatsApp — no message, chat, contact, credential or key —
   and nothing is sent unless you press Send.

sections.title: Plain-language summary
sections.text:
5. **Leviro Support, if you send a crash report** — a crash or a web error is
   written to a report file inside the app's own data directory, where it stays
   until **you** open the panel and press Send on that one report. Nothing is
   sent automatically and nothing is retried on its own. A report holds the
   error type, a sanitized message and stack, an optional screen id, the app and
   device fields listed in section 2a, and a few navigation breadcrumbs. It goes
   to Leviro Support through `levix.leviro.net/api/crash-reports`, a
   Levix-operated server; it is not forwarded to Telegram or any other service.
6. **The Levix mail relay, if you set a recovery email** — verifying the address
   in **Settings**, or choosing **Email** on **Forgot password**, posts the
   address and UI language (one of `en`, `ar`, `pt-BR`, `es-419`) to
   `levix.leviro.net/api/recovery-email`.
   The relay generates the verification code; confirming it sends the verification
   ID and your code and returns an address-bound recovery token. Password-reset
   requests send the address, locally generated code, token and language. The relay
   sends fixed code messages. It stores only keyed hashes and authorization state,
   never readable addresses, codes or tokens, and does not forward the address to
   the developer. Authorization expires after 365 days without an accepted reset;
   re-verifying the address revokes its previous authorization.
7. **Your own Levix instance, for a sticker** — when you tap **Make sticker** or
   **Add to stickers** on a file in Media Hub, that one file is uploaded to the
   Levix server running on this phone, because that is what does the conversion.
   It goes nowhere else. Browsing Media Hub uploads nothing.
8. **Translation and speech:** `!translate google` sends the text to
   `translation.googleapis.com` with your Google Translation API key, or to
   Google's public `translate.googleapis.com/translate_a/single` endpoint
   without a key. `!tts` and the AI `speak` tool send text to
   `translate.google.com` for speech generation.
9. **Weather, prayer times and short links:** `!weather` sends the city name
   you type to `api.openweathermap.org` when you configured its API key.
   `!prayer` sends the city name you type to `api.aladhan.com`. Levix never
   reads the device's location and requests no location permission; the only
   place information is the city name you type into these two commands. `!shortlink` sends the URL to
   `is.gd`, then to `v.gd` if the first service fails.
10. **Optional page and media fetches:** enabling link previews lets Levix
    request the host of a URL in an outgoing message to build a preview.
    Enabling remote thumbnails lets Levix download a remote media URL from its
    host to build a thumbnail. Both settings are off by default. These requests
    accept public HTTPS URLs only; every redirect is validated, and HTTP,
    credentials in URLs and private/loopback destinations are refused. A refused
    preview does not prevent sending the text message. Actual remote media sends
    use the same validation and the configured remote media size/time limits;
    the downloaded bytes are reused for the send and thumbnail.
11. **Model discovery and domain setup:** when you request live model
    discovery in the panel, the chosen provider's models endpoint receives
    your API key. On a desktop or server, `levix domain` requests
    `api.ipify.org` to check the server's public IP. If you approve installing
    Caddy, the installation may contact `dl.cloudsmith.io` and your system's
    package repositories. This command is not part of the Android app.

The database, settings, API keys, memory files and control panel are stored in
the app's private storage on Android. An API key also goes to its configured
provider when you use that provider or request live model discovery.

**Backups** (Settings → Backup) are local files created only when you ask. Every

sections.title: Plain-language summary
sections.text:
exported backup is encrypted with a password you choose (scrypt and
AES-256-GCM); Levix cannot recover that password.
Levix never uploads a backup to the developer or a cloud service. A backup can
contain bot settings, command setup, API keys, AI persona, conversations,
memory, schedules and their media, group data, roles and stickers. It never
contains WhatsApp pairing credentials, the panel password or session key,
recovery email, the install encryption key, device settings, logs, crash
reports or Android preferences. You control where the exported file is saved;
on Android it goes through the system's save and open pickers. A restore first
shows what it changes and asks you to confirm before it overwrites anything.
It writes only what the backup holds: settings, API keys or a persona the
backup lacks keep their current values, and it never changes the panel
password, the recovery email or the WhatsApp pairing. Conversations, memory and
other account data wait until the same WhatsApp account is linked.

---

sections.title: 1. Data stored locally
sections.text:
| Data | Where it lives | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WhatsApp pairing credentials | App-private SQLite DB + files | Linking to your WhatsApp account |
| Control-panel password | scrypt hash in the local DB | Logging into the local panel |
| Recovery email and authorization token | Sealed with AES-256-GCM in the local DB (`auth:recovery-email`) | A verified address for the panel's forgot-password email code. The panel shows a mask. Settings export does not include it. Unlink does not remove it |
| AI provider API keys & endpoints | Local DB, sealed with AES-256-GCM | Calling the provider you chose |
| Bot configuration (prefix, permissions, group settings) | Local DB | Running the bot |
| AI conversation history | Local DB (`ai_history`) | Conversational context; wiped with `!del` / `!delall` |
| Long-term AI memory | `memory/*.md` files in app storage | Facts you asked the bot to remember |
| Todos, notes, debts, schedules, warnings, user roles | Local DB | The bot's own features |
| Auto-delete rules | Local DB (`auto_delete_rules`) | Keyword auto-delete configuration |
| Opt-in copies of auto-deleted messages (text/caption only) | Local DB (`auto_delete_log`, auto-expiring) | Only when a rule with keep-copy on actually deletes a message |
| Forward counters and sender last-seen metadata | Local DB (auto-expiring) | The anti-forward feature |
| Crash reports (not yet sent) | App-private `crash-reports/*.json` (auto-expiring) | Optional diagnostics you can review and send; nothing leaves until you press Send |
| Logs (including the 14-day technical debug log) | App-private `logs/` + Android Logcat | Debugging |

Notes:

- The bot does **not** archive other people's messages by default. Nothing
  incoming is stored beyond the metadata rows listed above; deleted/edited
  messages are not captured. The one exception is an auto-delete rule with
  keep-copy turned on: it stores the text or caption (never media bytes) of
  messages that rule actually deleted, and those rows expire.
- Some data stored locally — especially AI conversation history, long-term
  memory, names and WhatsApp identifiers — can be included as context in a
  later AI request when you choose to use an AI feature. Local storage does
  not mean that this context can never leave the device.
- Android backup of app data is **disabled** (`allowBackup="false"`), so none
  of this is copied to Google's device backup.
- On Android, the embedded panel listens on a private socket file in app
  storage; only the app's WebView reaches it through the Android host. It does
  not open a TCP port. On desktop, server and Docker installs, the panel
  listens on every interface (`0.0.0.0`) by default unless `bind_address` is
  set. `levix domain` sets that address to `127.0.0.1` behind its reverse
  proxy. Android permits cleartext traffic only for the built-in panel origin;
  external endpoints use HTTPS.

sections.title: 2. Data that leaves the device, and to whom
sections.text:
| Recipient | What is sent | When | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **WhatsApp (Meta)** | Your messages, media you send through the bot, your phone number / pairing credentials, group metadata | Continuously while the bot is linked | Levix is a WhatsApp client; this is the product's core function |
| **Your configured AI provider** (Google, OpenAI-compatible server, or Anthropic — chosen by you, using your own API key) | The AI prompt and relevant context, which can include display name, WhatsApp user/phone identifiers, group name, messages, quoted/mentioned participant identifiers, AI history or memory, and supported media/files | Only when you invoke an AI feature (`!gemini`, `!ask`, `!ai`, `!generate`, `!stt`, …) | To generate or process the result you asked for |
| **Google Search grounding within Gemini** | A search Gemini chooses from the prompt already sent to Gemini | When Gemini decides to search during an AI request; `ai_google_search` is on by default for Gemini and can be turned off | Grounding an answer in current information |
| **DuckDuckGo** (`html.duckduckgo.com`) or **Google Programmable Search** (if you configured it) | The search query | When an AI answer uses `web_search` or `search_news`; the latter uses the same search path | Web-grounded answers and news |
| **Wikipedia** (`ar.wikipedia.org` or `en.wikipedia.org`) | The search query and matching page titles requested for summaries | When an AI answer uses `search_wikipedia` | Finding and reading articles |
| **Web pages the AI opens** | HTTPS request for the page to its host | When an AI answer uses `fetch_url` | Reading a page you asked about |
| **Google Cloud Translation** (`translation.googleapis.com`) | Text to translate and the configured Google Translation API key | When you use `!translate google` with a key | Translating text through the official API |
| **Google's public Translate endpoint** (`translate.googleapis.com/translate_a/single`) | Text to translate | When you use `!translate google` without a key | Translating text without an API key |
| **Google TTS** (`translate.google.com`) | Text to speak | When you use `!tts` or the AI uses `speak` | Generating speech |
| **Configured Gemini image endpoint** | The image prompt | When you use `!generate` or explicitly request an image through the AI `generate_image` tool, with the same command permission | Generating image bytes; it does not change the chat provider |
| **Configured Gemini/OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint, then your selected chat provider** | The selected attached/quoted voice audio goes to the transcription endpoint; the transcript goes to the chat provider and local AI history | When you request transcription through `transcribe_audio`, with the `stt` permission | Preparing a transcription and the AI answer; no unrelated chat audio is collected |
| **Local bundled documentation index** | No network request for retrieval; the returned public excerpts join the current AI request | When the AI uses `search_levix_docs` or `open_levix_doc_section` | Versioned product help; the index excludes agent instructions, private memories, settings and arbitrary files |
| **OpenWeatherMap** (`api.openweathermap.org`) | The city name and configured API key | When you use `!weather` with `openweathermap_api_key` set | Getting weather for the named city |
| **Aladhan** (`api.aladhan.com`) | The city name | When you use `!prayer` | Getting prayer times for the named city |
| **URL shorteners** (`is.gd`, then `v.gd` on fallback) | The URL to shorten | When you use `!shortlink` | Creating a short link |
| **Host of a URL in an outgoing message** | Request for the linked page | When `link_previews_enabled` is on and an outgoing message contains a previewable link; off by default | Building a link preview |

sections.title: 2. Data that leaves the device, and to whom
sections.text:
| **Host of a remote media URL** | Request to download the media | When remote media is sent, or when `thumbnail_remote` is enabled for a thumbnail | Sending media or building a thumbnail |
| **Configured AI provider's models endpoint** | The operator's API key | When the operator requests live model discovery in the panel | Listing available models |
| **IP lookup service** (`api.ipify.org`) | An IP lookup request, exposing the server's source IP | When the operator runs `levix domain` on a desktop or server; not an Android flow | Checking the server's public IP |
| **Caddy package sources** (`dl.cloudsmith.io` and system package repositories) | Package and repository requests, exposing the server's source IP | If the operator approves installing Caddy through `levix domain` | Installing the reverse proxy |
| **Your configured outbound proxy** (optional, off by default) | WhatsApp traffic only | While linked, if you set a proxy | Routing |
| **Leviro Support** (via `levix.leviro.net/api/feedback`; currently delivered to Leviro Support through **Telegram**, which carries and stores the message) | Only the feedback form's own fields — your message, the topic, an optional rating, an optional contact, an optional file you attach yourself — plus the Levix version, the platform, and the sending app's user-agent. If you tick the diagnostics box, the section 2a diagnostics object and the sanitized technical debug log in section 2b as well | Only when you press Send in **Settings → Feedback** | Support: so a bug you report or a request you make reaches the person who can act on it |
| **Leviro Support** (via `levix.leviro.net/api/crash-reports`, a Levix-operated server) | One crash report: category, sanitized error type/message/stack, an optional screen id, the app + section 2a device fields, the sanitized technical debug log in section 2b, and a few navigation breadcrumbs. Never a phone number, JID, chat/message body or media file | Only when **you** open the panel and press Send on one report; never automatically | Support: so a crash can be grouped and fixed |
| **Levix mail relay** (`levix.leviro.net/api/recovery-email`) | The recovery address and UI language; verification ID and entered verification code on confirmation; address, reset code, recovery token and language on reset. No free text | When you verify an address in **Settings**, or when you choose **Email** on **Forgot password** | To verify address ownership and authorize delivery. Only keyed hashes and authorization state persist, never readable addresses, codes or tokens; the address is not forwarded to the developer |
| **Your own Levix instance** (on Android, reached inside the app through a private socket; never the developer or an AI provider) | The one image, GIF or video you picked in Sticker Studio or the Media Hub, as a single upload | Only when you choose it in Sticker Studio or tap **Make sticker** / **Add to stickers** | Sticker Studio works in the local host, so it has to receive the file you chose |

Apart from feedback and crash reports you deliberately send to Leviro Support,
the developer of Levix is **not** a recipient of any of the above. The recovery-email relay
receives the fixed verification and reset fields described above. It stores only
keyed hashes and authorization state, never readable addresses, codes or tokens. The AI provider's use of the content you send
it is governed by that provider's own privacy policy.

sections.title: 2a. Optional feedback diagnostics and crash reports
sections.text:
Neither of these carries an identifier that follows your device. Report ids are
random, generated per report, and mean nothing outside that one report.

**Feedback diagnostics** — optional, with its own checkbox on the feedback
form. When you tick **Attach device & technical diagnostics**, the panel sends
exactly the object below, after the server has validated and trimmed it, plus
the technical debug log in section 2b. The panel shows this same list — field
and value — and the log under **See exactly what is sent** before you press
Send, so what you see is what is sent.

| Field | Example | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | `1` | the server, always |
| `levix` | `4.9.0` | the server, always |
| `node` | `v24.19.0` | the server, always |
| `platform` | `android` / `docker` / `node-linux` / `sea-linux` | the server, always |
| `nativeApp` | `4.9.0 (67)` | the Android app |
| `android` | `15 (API 35)` | the Android app |
| `device` | `samsung SM-A556E` | the Android app |
| `abi` | `arm64-v8a` | the Android app |
| `webview` | `131.0.6778.135` | the Android app |
| `screen` | `412x915@2.63` | the panel page |
| `language` | `ar` / `en` / `pt-BR` / `es-419` | the panel page |
| `theme` | `light` / `dark` | the panel page |
| `connectivity` | `wifi` / `cellular` / `ethernet` / `vpn` / `none` / `unknown` | the Android app |
| `memory` | `ok` / `low` / `unknown` | the Android app |
| `storage` | `ok` / `low` / `unknown` | the Android app |

Unknown values are the string `unknown`. A standalone browser has no Android
fields at all; they are simply not sent. Unticking the box means the request
carries no diagnostics key. It never contains your phone number, IMEI, Android
ID, advertising ID, IP address, location, Wi-Fi SSID, contacts, chat or message
text, JIDs, API keys, tokens or passwords. The one extra thing that accompanies
a ticked box is the sanitized technical debug log described in section 2b,
when the preview that froze it is still valid.

**Crash reports** — optional, one Send per report. A crash report is written
locally when the Node server dies on a fatal error, when the Android app
crashes, or when the panel hits a web error, and it holds:

- the schema version, a random per-report id, and a fingerprint used only to
  group reports that share a cause (not to identify a device);
- the timestamp and category (`node-uncaught`, `node-rejection`,
  `android-crash`, `android-anr`, `android-native`, `web-error`,
  `web-rejection`, `react-render`);
- the error type, a sanitized message, and up to 20 sanitized stack frames;
- an optional screen id — a route name only, never a URL or a query;
- the app fields (`levix`, `node`, `platform`, and `nativeApp` when known) and
  the same device fields as the diagnostics table above;
- up to 20 navigation breadcrumbs, each a kind, a time and an identifier.

A report's message, every stack frame and every breadcrumb name is scrubbed the
same way when the report is written and again before it is sent: WhatsApp JIDs
become `<jid>`, e-mail addresses `<email>`, runs of 7 or more digits `<number>`,
a URL keeps only its scheme and host, a 24+ character key-like run becomes
`<secret>`, and absolute paths under the data directory or your home become
`<data>` / `~`.
No phone number, IMEI, Android ID, advertising ID, IP address, location,
Wi-Fi SSID, contacts, chat or message bodies, JIDs, screenshots, API keys,
tokens or passwords are ever included. A Send carries the sanitized
technical debug log the preview froze (section 2b). The report's preview shows
that exact upload — log included — before you press Send. A missing or expired
preview sends the report with no debug log.

sections.title: 2b. Technical debug log
sections.text:
Levix keeps an internal, detailed debug log on the device to make a problem
diagnosable. It is one JSON-lines file per day in the app's private storage
(`logs/debug/`). Both previews in the panel show it under its own collapsed
heading before anything is sent.

**What it records:** the application's own operational events — connection and
session transitions, scheduled work, HTTP route activity, errors and stack
frames, with timestamps and levels. **What it never records:** message content,
media, WhatsApp JIDs, phone numbers, e-mail addresses, API keys, tokens,
passwords, cookies, session values or paths that name your install or home
directory. Every record is rebuilt before it is written: a secret-shaped field
name keeps only `[redacted]`, a message-content field keeps only its length (for
example `[redacted 42 chars]`), and every other string is scrubbed with the same
rules as a crash report (`<jid>`, `<email>`, `<number>`, `<secret>`, `<data>`,
`~`) and capped at 2000 characters. A day's file stops at 5 MB.

**Retention and deletion:** the device keeps 14 days, then the file is deleted
automatically. **Clear logs** in the panel deletes the debug log together with
the normal logs.

**When it leaves the device:** only in the two situations you start — feedback
sent with **Attach device & technical diagnostics** ticked, or a crash report
you press Send on. It is never sent on its own. The preview freezes the exact
string for 15 minutes. Send attaches that frozen copy. A missing or expired
preview attaches no debug log, never a newer one written after the preview.

sections.title: 3. Permissions the Android app requests
sections.text:
| Permission | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `INTERNET`, `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE` | WhatsApp connection and the local panel |
| `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` + `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE` | Keep the bot host running so the bot stays connected (special-use subtype: persistent personal WhatsApp bot host) |
| `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` | The ongoing connection-status notification |
| `WAKE_LOCK` | Keep the CPU awake while processing in the background |
| `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED` | Resume the host after device reboot |
| `REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` | Offer (never silently apply) a battery-optimization exemption so Android doesn't kill the host |
| `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`, `READ_MEDIA_VIDEO`, `READ_MEDIA_AUDIO` (Android 13+) | Discover and display WhatsApp media in the native Media Hub, only after you choose to grant access there |
| `READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED` (Android 14+) | Allow the Media Hub to show only photos and videos you select |
| `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` (Android 12 and earlier) | Discover WhatsApp media in the native Media Hub on older Android versions |

The Media Hub can also request read-only access to a WhatsApp Media folder through Android's folder picker when hidden statuses or documents are unavailable through MediaStore. It retains that local grant until you revoke it. Browsing, search, thumbnails, favorites, Storage Insights, saving copies, and deleting Levix-saved copies are all local to the device. The Media Hub makes no network requests and does not send media, file names, or folder structure to Levix or to an AI provider. Sharing a file happens only when you explicitly choose an app in Android's share sheet.

sections.title: Sticker Studio
sections.text:
**A file you pick stays on the device.** Browsing Media Hub, and having an item
offered as a sticker, are entirely local: nothing is uploaded just because you
scrolled past a photo or long-pressed it.

A file is handed over when you choose it in Sticker Studio or tap **Make sticker** or
**Add to stickers** for that one file. It then goes to **your own Levix server**
(the instance running on this phone), and nowhere else: not to the developer, not
to an AI provider, not to any third-party service. Sticker Studio needs the file
server-side to convert and to send, and your instance is the server. From there
the sticker goes to WhatsApp only if you send it, which is the same as any
message you send through Levix.

Two smaller points about the file while it is being handled:

- The handover is **one-shot and in memory**. The app records only a reference to
  the file it already has permission to read; it is not copied or cached, and it
  is streamed to the local server only when you upload it. A preview reads it
  through a short-lived local URL. Nothing about your photo is written to an
  app staging area, and the reference disappears when the app process ends.
- Files you **share out** of Sticker Studio are temporary copies in the app's
  private cache, and only of the formats Sticker Studio produces (WebP, PNG,
  GIF, MP4, or a pack ZIP). They are deleted automatically after a day. Choosing
  where a shared file goes is the share sheet's job — the app grants a read
  permission to the app *you* pick and nothing more.

No location, camera, microphone, contacts, SMS, or unrestricted storage permissions are
requested. Levix never collects the device's location. The in-app WebView loads only the local control panel
(`http://127.0.0.1:3001`); it does not load third-party web content.

sections.title: 4. Data retention and deletion
sections.text:
- **AI conversation history** — delete per chat with `!del` (or all chats with
  `!delall`, owner only), or from the panel.
- **Long-term memory** — `!memory forget` / `!memory clear`, or from the panel.
- **Unlink WhatsApp** (Connection → Unlink) — clears the WhatsApp credentials,
  roles, AI history, long-term memory and buffered context, and pauses the old
  account's schedules. The panel password and the recovery email are panel
  security, not WhatsApp data, and stay in place.
- **Recovery email** — removed from the device with **Remove** in **Settings**.
  It is sealed locally. The mail relay does not keep the address beyond rate
  limiting. `levix reset-password` does not remove it either.
- **Uninstall the app** — removes everything; there is no server-side copy of
  any of your data to survive deletion.
- **Feedback you chose to send** — it is a message in Leviro Support's Telegram
  chat, not a record in a Levix database, and the app has no copy of it. Ask
  Leviro Support to delete it (section 9) and it will be deleted from that chat.
- **Crash reports** — an unsent report stays on your device and is deleted
  automatically seven days after it is created (at most the 20 newest are kept);
  you can also delete any report, or all of them, from the panel at any time.
  A report you send is kept on the Levix crash-report server for at most 30 days
  and then deleted; ask Leviro Support to delete a sent one by its report id
  (section 9) and it will be deleted.
- **A file picked for a sticker** — the handover is in-memory and one-shot, so
  nothing to delete: once the panel reads it, the app has no copy left. It lives
  on afterwards only inside your own Levix server's data directory, alongside
  your other Levix data, and goes when you unlink WhatsApp or uninstall.
- **A sticker you shared out** — a temporary copy in the app's private cache,
  swept automatically once it is more than a day old.

sections.title: 5. Security
sections.text:
- API keys and auth blobs are sealed at rest with AES-256-GCM under an
  install-local key; the panel only ever reports whether a key is configured,
  never its value.
- The panel password is stored as a scrypt hash; login is throttled.
- The recovery email and its authorization token are sealed together with the
  same install key. The panel and login page show only a mask, never the address
  or token. Settings exports exclude both.
- Provider base URLs are validated on save and on use: public endpoints must
  be HTTPS, and private/reserved/metadata addresses are rejected (explicit
  loopback is allowed for local Ollama/LM Studio servers).
- Levix-owned fetch clients pin the validated DNS answer to the socket and
  follow redirects manually. The AI `fetch_url` tool accepts HTTPS only, and
  redirects are re-validated so a page cannot downgrade the request to HTTP.

sections.title: 6. Children
sections.text:
Levix is not directed at children. The Levix Android app is intended for users
aged **16 and over**. In Google Play Console, the target audience should be
declared as **16–17** and **18 and over**; age groups under 16 should not be
selected. Users must also meet WhatsApp's minimum-age requirements applicable
in their country or region.

sections.title: 7. Google Play Data Safety form — answer map
sections.text:
Fill the Play Console **App content → Data safety** form as follows. This
mapping reflects the Android app's current behavior and the categories used by
Google Play.
This file is the answer map; it does not change the Play Console, and the owner
updates the Console after review.

**Q: Does your app collect or share any of the required user data types?**
→ **Yes**

**Q: Is all of the user data collected by your app encrypted in transit?**
→ **Keep the existing No answer pending the final v5.0.0 transit audit.** The
previous HTTP paths in link previews and remote thumbnails are now blocked,
including redirects from HTTPS to HTTP. Outbound remote media URLs use the same
HTTPS-only boundary. These fixes alone do not establish an app-wide Yes: the
release audit must still examine other clients, redirects and supported local
provider/panel connections. This PR does not change the Play Console answer;
the owner reviews it before publishing v5.0.0.

**Account creation**
→ **My app does not allow users to create an account**

**Can users log in with accounts created outside of the app?**
→ **No**

**Q: Do you provide a way for users to request that their data is deleted?**
→ **No**. Levix has no developer-operated account or cloud copy to delete.
Users can still delete locally stored data with the in-app controls described
in section 4, unlink WhatsApp, or uninstall the app. Remove in Settings deletes
the recovery email and token from the device. The relay retains only keyed
hashes and authorization state subject to expiry, never the readable address.
Feedback a user chose to send is held in Leviro Support's Telegram chat; crash
reports a user chose to send are held for at most 30 days and then deleted. Both
are deleted on request through the contact in section 9.

| Personal info → **User IDs / personal identifiers** | Yes | No | Required | App functionality |
| Personal info → **Phone number** | Yes | No | Required | App functionality |
| Personal info → **Email address** | Yes | No | Optional | App functionality, Customer support |
| Location → **Approximate location** | Yes | No | Optional | App functionality |
| Messages → **Other in-app messages** | Yes | No | Optional | App functionality, Customer support |
| Photos and videos → **Photos** | Yes | No | Optional | App functionality, Customer support |
| Photos and videos → **Videos** | Yes | No | Optional | App functionality, Customer support |
| Audio files → **Voice or sound recordings** | Yes | No | Optional | App functionality |
| Audio files → **Other audio files** | Yes | No | Optional | App functionality, Customer support |
| Files and docs → **Files and docs** | Yes | No | Optional | App functionality, Customer support |
| Contacts → **Contacts** | Yes | No | Optional | App functionality |
| App activity → **In-app search history** | Yes | **Yes** | Optional | App functionality |
| App activity → **Other user-generated content** | Yes | **Yes** | Optional | App functionality |
| Web browsing → **Web browsing history** | Yes | **Yes** | Optional | App functionality |
